newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says operation in line with Sept 95 commitment.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says operation in line with Sept 95 commitment.

text.p: The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) neutral operation this morning was in line with the commitment the bank announced on September 8, 1995, a BOJ official told Reuters on Monday.
The official also said that Monday's rise in the key overnight call rate was due to banks' seasonal fund-raising demand ahead of the end of the fiscal year.
"We have been conducting operations within the commitment announced in September 1995," said the BOJ official.

When the central bank last cut the discount rate, at which it lends to other banks, on September 8, 1995, it also said it would guide the key overnight call rate slightly below the discount rate on average.
The discount rate was then halved to the current record low 0.5 percent.

Against market expectations of an accommodative operation, the BOJ injected 100 billion yen into the money market on Monday, which was just enough to offset a market shortfall of an estimated 90 billion yen.
This resulted in a rise in the key overnight call rate to 0.57 percent, the highest weighted average rate seen since the BOJ cut the discount rate in September 1995.
Friday's weighted average rate was 0.53 percent.
